categories.main_business_segments: Farasis Energy (Gan Zhou) Co., Ltd. primarily engages in the research, development, production, and sales of lithium-ion power batteries and battery systems, focusing on advanced large soft-pack laminated batteries. The company also develops and sells battery management systems, charging systems, electric vehicle auxiliary systems, and recycles used lithium batteries. It serves both automotive and energy storage sectors with products including ternary, lithium iron phosphate, and sodium-ion batteries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary technologies such as Super Punch Solution (SPS) large soft-pack battery systems, high-performance LMFP batteries, super-fast charging LFP batteries, and advanced semi-solid and solid-state battery technologies. It employs innovative manufacturing processes including high-speed stacking, laser welding, and digital simulation platforms. The production is based on a flexible manufacturing platform compatible with multiple battery chemistries and shapes, emphasizing cost reduction, safety, and performance.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include major domestic and international automotive manufacturers such as Mercedes-Benz, GAC Group, Dongfeng, Geely, and overseas clients like TOGG and Mahindra Group. The company serves the new energy vehicle market, energy storage applications, electric two-wheelers, eVTOL aircraft, and emerging sectors like humanoid robots and low-altitude economy vehicles. Over half of its revenue is derived from overseas markets, with a strong presence in Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China with production bases in Ganzhou, Guangzhou, Wuhu, Tianjin, and Kunming. It has established overseas operations including a 6GWh capacity joint venture in Turkey (Siro) and R&D centers in the US and Germany. Its sales and service network covers domestic and international markets, with significant exports to Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: Farasis Energy operates mainly in the midstream segment of the lithium-ion battery supply chain, focusing on battery cell manufacturing, module and pack assembly, and battery system integration. It also engages in upstream activities such as research and development of battery materials and downstream activities including battery recycling and energy storage solutions, positioning itself as a comprehensive energy solution provider.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes R&D in high-energy density, high-safety solid-state and semi-solid-state batteries, fast-charging LFP batteries, and sodium-ion batteries. It follows a 'produce one generation, reserve one generation, develop one generation' innovation strategy, with active development in AI-enabled battery management systems and digital simulation platforms. Strategic focus includes scaling SPS production, accelerating solid-state battery commercialization, expanding overseas markets, and entering emerging sectors like humanoid robots and low-altitude economy vehicles.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct sales of lithium-ion battery cells, modules, and battery packs to automotive manufacturers and energy storage customers. The company also earns income from related services such as battery management systems and recycling. Sales are conducted mainly via direct contracts and framework agreements with OEMs and strategic partners, with a significant portion of revenue from exports.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Farasis Energy is among the global leaders in soft-pack lithium-ion power batteries, ranking top three worldwide in soft-pack battery installations and first in China for soft-pack passenger vehicle batteries. It ranks eighth in overseas power battery installations and third in battery export volume in China. Competitors include other major Chinese and international battery manufacturers, but Farasis distinguishes itself with advanced soft-pack technology and strong overseas market penetration.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the company reported revenue of approximately RMB 11.68 billion, a 28.94% decrease from the previous year, primarily due to raw material price declines and customer structure optimization. Despite revenue decline, net loss narrowed significantly to RMB -332 million from RMB -1.87 billion in 2023. Total assets stood at RMB 26.63 billion with a net asset value of RMB 9.91 billion. The company is in a growth phase with ongoing capacity expansions and strategic overseas investments.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Farasis Energy emphasizes its advanced large soft-pack laminated battery technology (SPS) that offers high integration, safety, and space efficiency, enabling superior vehicle design flexibility. Its products combine high energy density, fast charging, long cycle life, and cost-effectiveness. The company’s globalized R&D and manufacturing capabilities, coupled with a flexible production platform compatible with multiple chemistries, provide strong competitive advantages in emerging markets and new application scenarios such as eVTOL and humanoid robots.
